cards.text: Friend, Israel is at war with the Ammonites, and the people of Gilead just made Jephthah their leader and commander. He sent the Ammonite king a long message, and the king paid it no attention. Like a paragraph in the group chat that gets NOTHING back, not even a thumbs up.

cards.question: Jephthah is about to move against the Ammonites. First, what comes upon him?

answers.text: A deep sleep from the LORD

cards.text: He passes through Gilead and Manasseh, then Mizpah of Gilead, and advances on the Ammonites. And he makes a vow to the LORD: "If indeed You will deliver the Ammonites into my hand,"

cards.question: Jephthah's vow goes on. If the LORD gives him the win, what does he say will belong to the LORD?

answers.text: Whatever comes out his door to greet him
The first lamb born in his flock
A tenth of what he takes in battle

cards.question: Jephthah vows to offer whatever comes out his door to greet him as a burnt offering.

cards.text: So Jephthah crosses over to fight the Ammonites. Now that big "if" in his vow is about to get its answer.

cards.question: In the fight, the Ammonites hold their ground against Jephthah.

cards.text: With a great blow he devastates twenty cities, and the Ammonites are subdued before the Israelites. Then Jephthah heads home to Mizpah, and the door of his house opens.

cards.question: Coming out the door to meet Jephthah, with tambourines and dancing, is his ___.
Jephthah has other children besides this daughter.

cards.text: The moment Jephthah sees her, he tears his clothes.

cards.question: Jephthah cries out, "No! Not my daughter!" Why does he say he can't take the vow back?

answers.text: He gave his word to the LORD
The elders of Gilead heard it
He swore it before his army

cards.text: Then his daughter answers him, "My father," and friend, what she says next takes my breath away.

cards.question: Jephthah's daughter tells him to ___ his word to the LORD, because the LORD has avenged him of the Ammonites.
Then Jephthah's daughter asks her father for one thing. What is it?

answers.text: Two months in the mountains with her friends
Two months at home with her father
Two months at Shiloh with the priests

cards.question: Up in the mountains with her friends, Jephthah's daughter goes to ___ her virginity.

cards.text: After two months, she returns to her father, and he does to her as he had vowed. She had never had relations with a man.

cards.question: After Jephthah does to his daughter as he vowed, a custom starts in Israel. What is it?

answers.text: Young women lament his daughter four days a year
Fathers stop making vows before a battle
Families dance with tambourines every spring

cards.text: This one's heavy, friend. And Jephthah's story isn't over yet.

findings.problem: No card says that the LORD gave Jephthah the victory (Judges 11:32, 'the LORD delivered them into his hand'). Card 6 says the 'if' in the vow is about to get its answer, but card 7 only asks whether the Ammonites held their ground, and card 8 only says Jephthah devastated twenty cities. The baker never learns that the LORD met the condition of the vow, and the rest of the story depends on that. The statement on card 7 could name the LORD as the one who delivers the Ammonites, or card 8 could tell it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This card is a flat list of place names followed by the first half of the vow, with nothing of Papa Dorin's voice. The march and the vow come before the tragedy, so this moment could carry a storyteller's line or some of his personality without muddying a fact.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, as the docs allow when the last verse is asked on a choice card. It tells nothing from any verse, but it still cites Judges 11:40.
findings.question: What should the verses field be on a closing card that is only the 'story isn't over' line? Should it repeat the last verse, be left empty, or be null? The rule says every story card cites the verses it tells, but this card tells none.
